claim: Paper lane; nothing about zeros of zeta. Twelve proved inequalities that consume a Hecke eigen-relation or exact local factor at every prime were catalogued (step using the eigen-relation, step using the functional equation, hypotheses) and the three zero-indexed objects substituted. No entry is met in full by a zero-indexed object at a zero in the open strip. Lemma T (proved): for a torus parameter every L(s,Pi,r x chi) is a product of shifted Dirichlet L-functions and rightmost pole minus rightmost local/gamma pole is 1 for every parameter and r; 'pole at 1' is equivalent to the conclusion with exponent 0. Proposition E: the Eisenstein-series proof of zeta(1+it)!=0 is the one entry met in full with a zero-specific hypothesis, at Re rho=1; in the strip the missing hypothesis is xi(2-rho)=0. For the weight-1/2 object every failing hypothesis is equivalent to beta=1/2 and not specific to zeros; theta-orthogonality is a hypothesis of no entry. For the resonance vector the eigen-relation fails (G26).
listStrictOnEdge: E10 x E*(z,rho/2) at Re rho = 1 (classical)
obstructionKind: every catalogued inequality with exponent below 1/2 needs L2, pole at 1, spectral membership or unitarity; for torus-parameter objects these are false at every parameter or equivalent to the target; zero-specific properties (single exponent, theta-orthogonality) are not what fails
lesson: A zero in the strip removes the constant-term coefficient whose argument is in the strip, never the one right of 1 (difference 1 in the L-argument); the template 'zero supplies cuspidality, a theorem contradicts it' is the classical proof on Re s = 1 and stops there. Inequalities that read an object through L(s,Pi,r x chi) cannot bound a torus parameter: pole and local pole move together for every r.
followUp: Independent referee owed. No explore device from this catalogue. A device would need a proved inequality without L2 / pole-at-1 / spectral membership / unitarity among its hypotheses and with a zero-specific hypothesis; on file only Maass-Selberg (G31), Lax-Phillips contraction (G26) and the edge theorem qualify, each reaching Re rho <= 1.
